sections.html:
Laurel is a city in Prince George's County on the Patuxent River, between Washington, D.C. and Baltimore. The population was 25,115 in 2010 and 30,060 in 2020. Most of the city is residential, and many residents commute to Washington or Baltimore. MARC Laurel Station on the Camden Line, Metrobus and RTA buses, U.S. 1, MD 198, I-95 and the Baltimore-Washington Parkway all serve the area, so list those links when you describe the house.

A Laurel mailing address does not always mean a Laurel city address. The city warns that ZIP codes 20707 and 20708 may fall in the county instead of the city, and that 20723 is Howard County and 20724 is Anne Arundel County. Check the parcel before you assume city rules apply to your house. The city has two wards, with MD 198 as the dividing line.

A Laurel homeowner pays one consolidated bill issued by Prince George's County, and it includes the city's tax. The city charges $0.71 per $100 of assessed value, and the county's fiscal 2026 real property rate is $1.0000 per $100 before its special rates.

Tax topicRule
Bill date and due dateBilled in July, due September 30

If a lender pays from escrow, the owner is still responsible, so confirm after any refinance or loan transfer. For questions about balances, call the city Budget and Personnel Services office at 301-725-5300, extension 2248.

Prince George's County's transfer tax is capped at 1.4%, and a 1% rate applies to certain principal residence sales to county classroom teachers and police officers. Your settlement company can tell you the rate on your closing.

sections.h2: City code violations before you sell
sections.html:
Check first whether the house has an open code violation, a rental license problem or a historic district rule attached to it. Each can slow a conventional sale.

  • Correction orders. The city issues a correction order before a fine. For vehicles, grass and weeds, and trash and debris it generally allows three days. Grass and weeds cannot exceed 8 inches, and unregistered or inoperable vehicles cannot be kept on a driveway. If an order is ignored, the city can do the work and place a lien.
  • Foreclosure notice. When a foreclosure is filed on residential property in the city, written notice goes to the city within five calendar days from the person authorized to make the sale.

The city also expects owners to clear snow within 12 hours after it stops and ice within 12 hours after it forms.

Owners of rental units need a city license at $40 per unit per year. Properties with fewer than 12 units are inspected every three years, and new participants get an initial inspection. Call the Fire Marshal and Permit Services office at 301-725-5300 before closing to ask how the license is handled in a sale and whether any inspection items are open.

The Laurel historic district is made up of seven contiguous districts in the north of the city, created around Main Street in 1975. Changes to a structure need a Certificate of Approval, and removing a tree visible from the street can need approval too. Older houses in the northern part of the city, many of them built around the old mill town, can carry design review. A buyer planning repairs should check this first.

Hurricane Agnes caused record flooding across Maryland in June 1972, and an F3-level tornado hit Laurel on September 24, 2001. Because the city sits along the Patuxent River, a house near the water deserves a closer look at drainage and basement moisture before it is listed or inspected.
Maryland sellers of homes with one to four units give the buyer a disclosure or disclaimer form. Hand it over early so the buyer cannot cancel for lateness, and keep a signed copy.

sections.h2: Where does a cash sale fit?
sections.html:
Sellers in Laurel most often face a house that is older, rented, inherited or behind on code or tax items. Those are the situations where preparing a listing costs more time than the owner has.

A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the buyer can close on your schedule and take the house as it stands. It does not remove the need to clear liens, resolve a rental license or confirm who has authority to sell an inherited property. Ask any buyer, in writing, how those items will be handled before you sign.

To compare routes, line up three numbers: what a listing would net after repairs and sale costs, how many months of carrying costs you can absorb, and what a written cash offer would net.

sections.h2: What to bring to a buyer conversation
sections.html:
• The latest consolidated tax bill, which shows both the county and city portions.
  • Any correction order, with proof that you fixed the problem.
  • The rental license and inspection record, for a leased house.
  • A Certificate of Approval for past exterior work, if the house is in the historic district.
  • The deed, or for an inherited house, the paperwork that shows who may sign.

Buyers move faster when these are in hand. A cash buyer has no lender waiting on documents, so the closing date mostly depends on how quickly your side answers and how fast the title search finishes.

sections.h2: Steps to close a Laurel sale
sections.html:
1. Pull the parcel to confirm the house is inside the city.
  2. Ask the city about open correction orders, rental inspection items and historic district status.
  3. Request a tax balance from the county, remembering that the city portion is on the same bill.
  4. Complete the disclosure or disclaimer form.
  5. At settlement, the title company pays any lien or balance from your proceeds and records the deed.

For an inherited house, add one step at the start: confirm who has authority to sign. If the county or city mails a notice while the house is under contract, send a copy to the title company right away so nothing is missed before settlement.

faqs.q: Is Laurel, MD in Prince George's County?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Laurel is in Prince George's County, though nearby addresses with a Laurel mailing address can sit in Howard County or Anne Arundel County. Check the parcel before assuming county or city rules.

faqs.q: When are Laurel property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property tax is billed in July and due September 30, with a semi-annual option for owner-occupied homes of half by September 30 and half by December 31. Payments after September 30 carry 1.667% a month.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Laurel?
faqs.a: The license applies to owners of rental units in the city, at $40 per unit per year, with an inspection for new participants. Call 301-725-5300 before closing to ask how it is handled in a sale.

faqs.q: Can the city fine me for tall grass or a junk vehicle before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Laurel issues a correction order first, generally with three days to fix grass over 8 inches, trash or an unregistered vehicle. If it goes unfixed, the city can do the work at your cost, add a lien or levy fines.

faqs.q: Does the Laurel historic district affect selling?
faqs.a: It can. Houses in the seven contiguous districts in the north of the city need a Certificate of Approval for changes to the structure, and tree removal visible from the street can need approval.
